title: Combinatorial polynomial-time algorithm for MWIS in perfect graphs
statement_text: Design a combinatorial polynomial-time algorithm for the Maximum Weight Independent Set problem in perfect graphs.
context_text: Given a graph with non-negative vertex weights, Maximum Weight Independent Set (MWIS) asks for an independent set of maximum total weight; it is NP-hard in general. A graph is perfect if the chromatic number of every induced subgraph equals its clique number; by the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem, equivalently, it has no odd hole (induced odd cycle of length at least 5) and no odd antihole (complement of one). Grötschel, Lovász and Schrijver gave a polynomial-time algorithm for MWIS in perfect graphs, but it relies on the ellipsoid method; a combinatorial algorithm means one avoiding such general convex-optimization machinery. The authors call the design of a combinatorial polynomial-time algorithm an important open problem. A related question, the existence of a combinatorial polynomial-time algorithm for Maximum Weight Clique in perfect graphs without long antiholes (equivalently MWIS in graphs with no hole of length at least 5 and no odd antihole), also received much attention; the authors give a polynomial-time algorithm for MWIS in all graphs with no hole of length at least 5 (long-hole-free graphs), via potential maximal cliques and a container method.
notes: Stated in prose without a labelled environment: 'Designing a combinatorial polynomial-time algorithm for MWIS in perfect graphs remains an important open problem.' A classical community-wide open problem acknowledged by the authors as ongoing context.
paper_title: Induced subgraphs of bounded treewidth and the container method

title: MWIS in P7-free graphs
statement_text: Determine the computational complexity of the Maximum Weight Independent Set problem in $P_7$-free graphs.
context_text: Given a graph with non-negative vertex weights, Maximum Weight Independent Set (MWIS) asks for an independent set of maximum total weight; it is NP-hard in general. $P_t$ is the path on $t$ vertices and a graph is $P_t$-free if it has no induced $P_t$. No NP-hardness result for MWIS is known in $P_t$-free graphs for any $t$. $P_4$-free graphs have bounded cliquewidth, so MWIS is solvable there in linear time; polynomial-time algorithms were found for $P_5$-free graphs (Lokshtanov, Vatshelle, Villanger, 2014) and $P_6$-free graphs (Grzesik, Klimošová, Pilipczuk, Pilipczuk, 2019), and the case of $P_7$-free graphs remains open. The authors show that, for graphs with no induced cycle of length at least 6 and no induced extended $C_5$ (a 5-cycle plus a vertex adjacent to one or two consecutive vertices of it), a maximum-weight induced subgraph of treewidth less than $k$ can be found in time $n^{O(k)}$; this class contains all $P_5$-free graphs, so it generalizes the $P_5$-free result and also gives Feedback Vertex Set in $P_5$-free graphs in polynomial time, but it does not cover $P_6$- or $P_7$-free graphs.
notes: Stated in passing prose: 'the case of P7-free graphs remains open.' No labelled theorem environment.
